terms.gloss: of a place: full of people, crowded
terms.comment: Of a place that is full of people at the moment (a theatre, the senate, a town). Under “frequent” the word has its other sense, “often present”.

evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.3.133: in forō celeberrimō, tantā frequentiā (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of a place where many people usually come: a busy spot, a busy square.

terms.grammar: with the ablative of what fills it: hominibus refertus
evidence: Cic. Q. Fr. 1.1.42: theātrum … celebritāte refertissimum

phrases.latin: Quanta turba! Forum hominibus refertum est.
phrases.english: What a crowd! The square is packed with people.

phrases.latin: Hīc locus nimis frequēns est; manum meam tenē.
phrases.english: It’s too crowded here; hold my hand.

phrases.latin: Vidētisne refertum forum populumque Rōmānum ad spem reciperandae lībertātis ērēctum?
phrases.english: Do you see the forum packed, and the Roman people roused to the hope of winning back their freedom?

phrases.latin: Id haud magnum quidem oppidum est, sed plūs quam mediterrāneum celebre et frequēns emporium.
phrases.english: It is not a large town, but a busier and more crowded market than you would expect inland.

sources: Lewis & Short: frequens · Lewis & Short: celeber · Lewis & Short: refercio
Cicero, Philippics 3.32; Letters to Atticus 12.23.3; Letters to his brother Quintus 1.1.42.
